caption: A magnet is lowered toward a pile of paperclips on a desk, and the clips jump up and cling to it.

sa.check: A pile of paperclips on a desk.
A magnet is lowered toward the pile.
The clips jump up and cling to the magnet.
The clips are loose in a pile, not in a box.
The lowering comes first and the jump follows.

pc.expect: The clips lie still until the magnet is close above them, then leap up to it; clips far from the magnet stay put, and the leaping stops when the magnet is taken away.
pc.fail: Clips jump while the magnet is still high above or off to one side; or clips across the desk slide toward the magnet; or clips move before the magnet has been lowered; or clips keep hopping after the magnet is well away.

pc.expect: Clips on the magnet hang from its underside and sides in chains, touching it or each other; any that drop off fall back to the desk.
pc.fail: Clips hover in the air between desk and magnet touching nothing; or a clip that lets go drifts upward or sideways; or clips rise past the magnet; or the chains stand straight up above the magnet.

pc.expect: Each clip moves along the line from its spot to the magnet and stops on it or on a clip already there; the chains travel with the magnet as it moves.
pc.fail: A clip flies past the magnet and off; or clips circle the magnet in the air; or chains stay hanging in place when the magnet is moved away; or clips bounce off and back several times.

pc.expect: The clips stay rigid bent wire; the magnet stays a hard block; the desk does not dent.
pc.fail: Clips bend or straighten as they jump; or melt together into a lump; or the magnet squashes; or the desk surface dents under the pile.

pc.expect: The clips on the magnet are the clips from the pile; none appear from nowhere or vanish; the magnet passes through nothing.
pc.fail: Clips multiply on the magnet; or clips vanish in mid-air; or the magnet passes into the desk; or two clips merge into one.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The magnet's colour and shape, the clips' colour and the desk stay the same.
pc.fail: The magnet changes colour or shape; or the clips change colour; or the desk's contents rearrange.
